scope: Four P2 distinct candidate groups from the frozen 54-card owner reconciliation. This supplements the preceding 11-candidate review; it does not close all partial or unmatched P1 observations.
rules: Preserve provisional candidate IDs and original editorial decisions.
No canonical IDs allocated; no app content, release flags or Calendar data changed.
Original bilingual paraphrases only; primary folklore records describe reported beliefs, not Catholic approval.
Feast dates indicate context; Calendar retains precedence and transfer decisions.

owner.decision: Preserve distinct historical craft candidate; do not merge with shamrock, St Brigid cross or St Patrick's Breastplate.

calendar.qualification: Civil celebration date does not settle occurrence of the liturgical feast or any Lenten dispensation.

sources.locator: Paragraphs on Thomas Dinely (1681), children's crosses and Dublin rosettes (1908)
sources.claim: Historical wearing of crosses and later paper/ribbon variants.
sources.limit: The page's broad statement about Lenten restrictions is not a source for applicable fasting law.

sources.locator: Historical discussion; late-1930s Schools' Collection quotations; Sources section
sources.claim: Children's domestic badges; decline by the late 1930s; museum-led craft revival.
sources.limit: A revival activity does not prove continuous present-day observance everywhere.

editorial_en.name: St Patrick's ribbon cross
editorial_en.geography: Historical Irish household practice, with regional designs.
editorial_en.history: Cross wearing is recorded in 1681. Later children's badges used card, ribbon or paper; museum research describes substantial decline by the late 1930s.
editorial_en.meaning: A decorative cross honours the saint and recalls Christian faith.
editorial_en.practice: Families made badges for children to wear on the feast, with varied colours and forms.
editorial_en.contemporary: An optional historical craft revival using materials already at home.
editorial_en.qualification: No obligatory design, sacramental status or automatic exemption from Lenten discipline is implied.

editorial_fr.name: La croix de rubans de saint Patrick
editorial_fr.geography: Usage familial irlandais historique, aux motifs régionaux variés.
editorial_fr.occasion: Le 17 mars, jour de la Saint-Patrick.
editorial_fr.history: Le port de croix est signalé en 1681. Les insignes d'enfants ultérieurs utilisaient carton, rubans ou papier ; les recherches muséales décrivent un net déclin à la fin des années 1930.
editorial_fr.meaning: La croix décorative honore le saint et rappelle la foi chrétienne.
editorial_fr.practice: Les familles confectionnaient des insignes que les enfants portaient le jour de la fête, selon des formes et couleurs diverses.
editorial_fr.contemporary: Une activité historique facultative, réalisable avec des matériaux déjà disponibles.
editorial_fr.qualification: Aucun motif obligatoire, statut de sacramental ou dispense automatique des règles du Carême n'est sous-entendu.

gaps: Exact first origin remains unknown; 1681 is a documented witness, not the invention date.
Local modern continuity needs separate evidence.
Gendered historical designs describe past practice rather than requirements.

owner.decision: Preserve one Irish Christmas candle candidate; distinguish table remembrance and window hospitality as local facets.

calendar.qualification: Christmas Eve is the vigil of the Nativity; lighting a household candle is optional.

sources.locator: Schools' Collection, volume 0506, p.062; Áth Dara (C.), Adare, Co. Limerick; Christmas Eve Customs
sources.claim: A local account records a window candle on Christmas Eve and Christmas night.
sources.limit: Local historical testimony, not nationwide prevalence or current practice.

sources.issuer: National Museum of Ireland; Clodagh Doyle, Irish Folklife Division
sources.locator: Christmas Eve/Christmas Day; cited P. J. O'Sullivan, Annascaul, Co. Kerry, 1941, UCD Ms.782:257
sources.claim: Historical remembrance candles and a dated Kerry table-candle witness.
sources.limit: Reported spirit-return and guaranteed-blessing beliefs are folklore, not instructions or verified supernatural events.

editorial_en.name: The Irish Christmas candle
editorial_en.geography: Irish households; distinct local witnesses include Adare in Limerick and Annascaul in Kerry.
editorial_en.occasion: Christmas Eve and Christmas night; household timing varied.
editorial_en.history: Folklore collections preserve twentieth-century accounts of candles at windows or on tables. The evidence does not establish the custom's first origin.
editorial_en.meaning: A light can accompany welcome for Christ and remembrance of loved ones.
editorial_en.practice: Households lit Christmas candles; some associated them with hospitality or deceased relatives.
editorial_en.contemporary: An optional family remembrance with a safe light and an existing Christmas or intercessory prayer.
editorial_en.qualification: Use an electric candle where appropriate. Historical beliefs about returning spirits or guaranteed favours are not taught as Catholic doctrine.

editorial_fr.name: La bougie de Noël dans les foyers irlandais
editorial_fr.geography: Foyers irlandais ; des témoignages locaux distincts proviennent notamment d'Adare, dans le Limerick, et d'Annascaul, dans le Kerry.
editorial_fr.occasion: La veille et la nuit de Noël, selon des horaires familiaux variables.
editorial_fr.history: Les collections folkloriques conservent des témoignages du XXe siècle sur des bougies aux fenêtres ou sur les tables. Ces sources n'établissent pas l'origine première de l'usage.
editorial_fr.meaning: Une lumière peut accompagner l'accueil du Christ et le souvenir des proches.
editorial_fr.practice: Les foyers allumaient des bougies de Noël, parfois liées à l'hospitalité ou aux parents défunts.
editorial_fr.contemporary: Un souvenir familial facultatif avec une lumière sans danger et une prière de Noël ou d'intercession existante.
editorial_fr.qualification: Préférer une bougie électrique si nécessaire. Les croyances historiques sur le retour des esprits ou les faveurs garanties ne sont pas enseignées comme doctrine catholique.

gaps: Migration of this custom to American Christmas practice remains unverified (WEI58-06-001 stays held).
No claim of uninterrupted modern national observance.
Hospitality, remembrance and supernatural folklore are related source themes, not interchangeable claims.

owner.decision: Retain separate local attestations; no universal bonfire rite, Breton maritime extension or automatic event.

calendar.traditional_date: Nativity of St John Baptist, 24 June; eve commonly 23 June
calendar.qualification: A nearby parish festival date does not move the 1962 feast; Oloron's announced 2026 event was 20 June.

sources.issuer: French public heritage inventory / Région Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
sources.locator: Notice IA04002601; enquiry 2006; Historique, processional oratory at Saint-André-les-Alpes
sources.claim: Documents a local parish sequence including Mass, statue procession, church blessing and a St John fire.
sources.limit: The oratory's probable nineteenth-century date is not a first date for the fire custom; no blessing text is identified.

sources.issuer: Diocese of Bayonne, Lescar and Oloron
sources.locator: Event announcement, 20 June 2026, Notre-Dame du Faget, Oloron-Sainte-Marie
sources.claim: Announces parish Mass, shared meal, bonfire, songs, stories and prayers.
sources.limit: An announcement demonstrates an organised event was offered, not independent proof it took place or will recur.

editorial_en.name: St John Baptist's community bonfire
editorial_en.geography: Named French parish examples in Saint-André-les-Alpes and Oloron-Sainte-Marie; their forms remain distinct.
editorial_en.occasion: Around the Nativity of St John Baptist on 24 June, according to an actual local announcement.
editorial_en.history: A French heritage survey records a parish procession and fire; a separate diocesan announcement documents a modern parish programme.
editorial_en.meaning: A Christian gathering may honour the saint who prepared Christ's way.
editorial_en.practice: Local programmes can combine worship, shared food, prayer, song and a community fire.
editorial_en.contemporary: Join an appropriately organised local event, or honour the saint with prayer at home.
editorial_en.qualification: No fire-building instructions or universal blessing rite; do not treat solstice festivals as automatically Catholic observances.

editorial_fr.name: Le feu communautaire de la Saint-Jean-Baptiste
editorial_fr.geography: Exemples paroissiaux français nommés à Saint-André-les-Alpes et à Oloron-Sainte-Marie, dont les formes restent distinctes.
editorial_fr.occasion: Autour de la Nativité de saint Jean-Baptiste, le 24 juin, selon une annonce locale réelle.
editorial_fr.history: Une enquête du patrimoine décrit une procession paroissiale suivie d'un feu ; une annonce diocésaine distincte présente un programme paroissial contemporain.
editorial_fr.meaning: Le rassemblement chrétien peut honorer le saint qui prépara la venue du Christ.
editorial_fr.practice: Les programmes locaux peuvent réunir culte, repas partagé, prière, chants et feu communautaire.
editorial_fr.contemporary: Participer à une fête locale convenablement organisée, ou honorer le saint par la prière à la maison.
editorial_fr.qualification: Aucune instruction pour allumer un feu ni rite universel de bénédiction ; les fêtes du solstice ne sont pas automatiquement des observances catholiques.

gaps: Breton fishermen's fires at sea and crew prayers remain unverified.
No exact pre-1962 blessing formula or ministerial permission established.
Origins and local continuity require site-specific evidence; announced 2026 programme is not an attendance report.

owner.decision: Preserve one candidate with separately named Polish pisanki and Ukrainian pysanky; do not duplicate BLSS-004 food blessing or treat Ukrainian heritage as exclusively Latin Catholic.

calendar.traditional_date: Easter season; no independently established universal Holy Saturday decorating time
calendar.qualification: Craft timing follows family custom; Calendar owns the date of Easter. Blessing and decoration are separate activities.

sources.claim: Documents Ukrainian wax-resist egg art, family transmission, Easter exchange and wider religious/cultural participation.
sources.limit: Heritage recognition does not approve protection beliefs or establish a Catholic origin; no first-origin date inferred.

sources.claim: Describes Polish pisanka and Ukrainian pysanka, wax-resist decoration and Easter gifts symbolising life.
sources.limit: Direct open returned 404 in this review; marked search-index-only corroboration, requiring URL recovery before release. Not relied upon for a ritual or exclusive Catholic identity.

sources.issuer: Muzeum Wsi Radomskiej / Radom Village Museum
sources.locator: Plastyka obrzędowa, paragraphs on pisanki/kraszanki/rysowanki/oklejanki and batik technique
sources.claim: Directly accessible Polish museum account distinguishes decorated-egg techniques and describes applying wax before dye.
sources.limit: Supports Polish regional craft; neither a 1962 blessing nor a precise origin date.

editorial_en.name: Decorating Easter eggs: pisanki and pysanky
editorial_en.geography: Polish and Ukrainian traditions, including diaspora communities; names, motifs and religious settings vary.
editorial_en.occasion: Easter and family preparations for the feast.
editorial_en.history: Regional egg art is transmitted in families; UNESCO documents the Ukrainian tradition, while museum material distinguishes Polish and Ukrainian names. Exact origins remain uncertain.
editorial_en.meaning: An Easter egg can suggest new life; individual motifs have varied cultural meanings.
editorial_en.practice: Families decorate and exchange eggs; some traditions use successive applications of wax and dye.
editorial_en.contemporary: An optional family art activity connected with Easter prayer, with local names and styles respected.
editorial_en.qualification: No protective or divinatory power is asserted. Decoration is distinct from an authorised food blessing and is not confined to Roman Catholics.

editorial_fr.name: Décorer les œufs de Pâques : pisanki et pysanky
editorial_fr.geography: Traditions polonaises et ukrainiennes, y compris dans les diasporas ; noms, motifs et contextes religieux varient.
editorial_fr.occasion: Pâques et les préparatifs familiaux de la fête.
editorial_fr.history: Cet art régional se transmet en famille ; l'UNESCO documente la tradition ukrainienne et des ressources muséales distinguent les noms polonais et ukrainiens. Les origines précises restent incertaines.
editorial_fr.meaning: L'œuf pascal peut évoquer la vie nouvelle ; chaque motif possède des significations culturelles variables.
editorial_fr.practice: Les familles décorent et offrent des œufs ; certains usages emploient des couches successives de cire et de teinture.
editorial_fr.contemporary: Une activité artistique familiale facultative, reliée à la prière pascale et respectueuse des noms et styles locaux.
editorial_fr.qualification: Aucun pouvoir protecteur ou divinatoire n'est affirmé. La décoration se distingue d'une bénédiction autorisée des aliments et n'appartient pas exclusivement aux catholiques romains.

gaps: Smithsonian legacy URL recovery remains a citation-maintenance task; the directly accessible Radom museum source independently supports Polish technique. Earliest origin and specific local Catholic reception remain open.
Do not infer Holy Saturday-specific painting, a universal recipe, fixed motif meanings or the 1962 blessing formula.
UNESCO's general pre-Christian-origin account is not evidence for a precise archaeological starting date.
